headline: Advance Boat and Campsite Planning for Bighorn Lake
reservation: Many Bighorn Canyon campsites are first come, first served; only a small number of South District sites are reservable through Horseshoe Bend Marina. Check the rules for your specific campground and current lake levels before arranging boat access.

days.title: Canyon Rims and Crimson Cliffs

stops.name: Devil Canyon Overlook
stops.detail: View the 1,000-foot vertical limestone drops where the Bighorn River carves a deep ribbon through the plateau.

stops.name: Sullivan Knob Trail
stops.detail: Hike this short path to experience the canyon's natural acoustics and narrowest viewpoints.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for park roads; conditions vary with weather.
days.note: Wind speeds on the rim can be high; secure hats and loose gear.

days.title: Pioneer History and High Desert Waters

stops.name: Lockhart Ranch
stops.detail: Explore the preserved 20th-century homestead of Caroline Lockhart, featuring over a dozen historic structures.

stops.name: Horseshoe Bend
stops.detail: Access the red-walled shoreline for kayaking or wading in the reservoir's silt-rich waters.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours for local park transit; conditions vary.
days.note: Ranch buildings are generally exterior-viewing only; check for seasonal ranger tours.

days.title: Wild Mustangs and Mountain Vistas

stops.name: Pryor Mountain Wild Horse Range
stops.detail: Look for the colonial Spanish-descended wild horse herd roaming the rugged sagebrush hills.

stops.name: Ewing-Snell Ranch
stops.detail: Visit this early settler site located near the southern park entrance to view the remains of a log home and forge.

days.driving: Allow 3 hours for unpaved terrain; conditions vary.
days.note: High-clearance vehicles are strongly recommended for the Pryor Mountain access roads.

intel.title: Marina Capacity
intel.text: Parking for boat trailers at Horseshoe Bend fills quickly on summer weekends; arrive early or visit midweek. Overflow areas are limited and require maneuvering through narrow lots.

intel.title: Deep Canyon Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular service is nonexistent within the canyon depths and highly spotty at overlooks. Download all maps and reservation confirmations before leaving Lovell.

intel.title: Gateway Supply Points
intel.text: There are no fuel stations within the Recreation Area boundaries. Ensure tanks are topped off in Lovell or Cody before entering the park.

intel.title: South vs North Access
intel.text: Note that no internal road connects the South District (WY) to the North District (MT). Allow at least 3 hours to drive around the Bighorn Mountains via regional highways.

intel.title: Water Level Constraints
intel.text: Boat ramp accessibility is strictly dependent on Bighorn Lake water elevations. Check the official NPS 'Current Conditions' page for daily updates on ramp closures.

plan.arrival: Collect rental vehicle at Yellowstone Regional Airport (COD), stock supplies in Cody or Lovell, and visit the Bighorn Canyon Visitor Center in Lovell for latest terrain updates.
plan.vehicle: High-clearance 4WD vehicles are recommended for Pryor Mountain roads; check rental agreements for off-pavement restrictions.
plan.goldenHour: Devil Canyon Overlook offers dramatic lighting as sun hits the limestone walls; season-dependent colors vary.
